candidate_rules.summary: Fast-to-slow clock domain single-cycle pulses must use a closed-loop toggle-handshake synchronizer with busy backpressure, never a direct 2-FF level synchronizer.
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: If destination clock period T_dst > source pulse width T_src, a single-cycle pulse in Domain A can assert and deassert completely between two rising edges of clkB, causing silent pulse loss. In burst mode, back-to-back pulses separated by less than 2*T_dst also coalesce unless a closed-loop busy_o handshake throttles the source FSM until the destination acknowledges receipt.

candidate_rules.summary: Asynchronous FIFO read/write pointers must be converted to Gray code and registered in the source domain before passing through 2-FF synchronizers.
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: Synchronizing a multi-bit binary counter directly across asynchronous clocks causes catastrophic pointer corruption because multiple bits flip simultaneously (e.g., 0111 -> 1000). Under interconnect skew and setup/hold metastability, the receiving domain samples a random combination of old and new bits. Gray code (bin ^ (bin >> 1)) guarantees unit Hamming distance (1 bit flip per increment).

candidate_rules.summary: Arbitrary multi-bit data buses crossing asynchronous domains must be held stable by the source register while a synchronized Req/Ack handshake completes.
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: Non-Gray multi-bit data words cannot be synchronized bit-by-bit. Instead, the source domain must latch the data word into a holding register (data_hold_q), assert a request level/toggle, wait for the destination 2-FF synchronizer to detect the request edge and safely sample data_hold_q, and wait for the synchronized acknowledge before updating data_hold_q.
candidate_rules.golden_template:
// [GOLDEN PATTERN] Stable Holding Register + Synchronized Request Edge Sampling
always_ff @(posedge clkA or negedge rst_n) begin
  if (!rst_n) begin data_hold_q <= '0; req_tog_q <= 1'b0; end
  else if (send_en && !busy_o) begin data_hold_q <= data_in; req_tog_q <= ~req_tog_q; end
end
always_ff @(posedge clkB or negedge rst_n) begin
  if (!rst_n) begin {req_b3, req_b2, req_b1} <= 3'b000; data_out_q <= '0; end
  else begin
    {req_b3, req_b2, req_b1} <= {req_b2, req_b1, req_tog_q};
    if (req_b2 ^ req_b3) data_out_q <= data_hold_q;
  end
end

candidate_rules.summary: Never feed combinational logic directly into a 2-FF synchronizer or reconverge two independent 2-FF synchronizers in the destination domain.
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: Combinational logic in the source domain produces transient hazards/glitches during input transitions; feeding a combinational net directly into a synchronizer allows clkB to sample a glitch pulse. Always register the signal in the source domain (clkA) immediately before the CDC boundary, and coalesce control conditions before crossing.

candidate_rules.summary: Every FSM next-state case statement must include an explicit default branch that returns state_d to ST_IDLE and deasserts outputs.
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: When an N-bit state register implements K < 2^N valid states, radiation-induced Single-Event Upsets (SEU) or power-on reset glitches can flip state_q into an unenumerated state. Without an explicit default transition to ST_IDLE, the controller locks up permanently until a hard power cycle.

candidate_rules.summary: FSM control strobes driving asynchronous boundaries, write enables, or downstream clocks must be Moore-registered or look-ahead registered to eliminate combinational glitches.
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: Combinational Mealy outputs depend on both state_q bits and external inputs. Because multi-bit state_q transitions have non-zero gate/wire skew, decoding logic can produce narrow sub-nanosecond hazard glitches that falsely trigger downstream FIFOs, memories, or CDC synchronizers.
candidate_rules.anti_pattern:
// [ANTI-PATTERN] Combinational Mealy decode prone to state-bit skew glitches
assign fifo_push_o = (state_q == ST_WRITE) && ready_i;
candidate_rules.sdc_constraint: N/A (Registered output maximizes downstream setup margin)

candidate_rules.summary: Separate FSM sequential registers (state_q in always_ff) from combinational next-state logic (state_d in always_comb) so COI and pre-posedge (t-1ps) waveform tables can isolate transition bugs.
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: Single-block FSMs (where next-state decoding and output assignments are buried inside a monolithic always_ff block) hide the combinational next-state net (state_d) from waveform inspection at t-1ps and often lead to accidental one-cycle pipeline latency mismatches on outputs.

candidate_rules.summary: Use one-hot state encodings with single-bit index comparisons when FSM decode delay dominates the critical path (ltp -noff).
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: Binary-encoded FSMs with many states require wide multi-bit equality comparators on every state branch, adding 2 to 4 levels of combinational gate delay before datapath muxes. One-hot encoding reduces state detection to a 1-bit wire tap.
candidate_rules.anti_pattern:
// Wide binary state comparison on critical control path
assign mux_sel_o = (state_q == 5'd19) || (state_q == 5'd23);
candidate_rules.golden_template:
// One-hot state bit indexing reduces comparator depth to 1 OR gate
assign mux_sel_o = state_onehot_q[ST_BIT_19] | state_onehot_q[ST_BIT_23];

candidate_rules.summary: Initialize all outputs and local variables at the top of always_comb before conditional branches to guarantee zero inferred latches ($dlatch).
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: When a signal assigned inside an always_comb block is not assigned a value on every possible execution path, Yosys and ASIC synthesis tools infer a level-sensitive transparent latch ($dlatch) to preserve the previous value. Latches introduce severe timing-borrowing race conditions, glitch propagation, and DFT scan untestability.
candidate_rules.anti_pattern:
always_comb begin
  if (en_i)
    y_o = data_i; // Missing else branch infers $dlatch!
end
candidate_rules.golden_template:
always_comb begin
  y_o = '0; // Upfront default initialization guarantees purely combinational logic
  if (en_i) begin
    y_o = data_i;
  end
end

candidate_rules.summary: Use explicit SystemVerilog width casts (e.g., WIDTH'(expr)) and sized literals to eliminate implicit bit-width truncation and expansion warnings.
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: Implicitly assigning a wider expression (such as an unsized integer literal 1 or an N+1 bit carry sum) to an N-bit target silently truncates MSBs, which can clip carry-outs, wrap array indices prematurely, and trigger Verilator WIDTHTRUNC/WIDTHEXPAND errors.
candidate_rules.anti_pattern:
logic [3:0] count_q;
always_ff @(posedge clk_i) count_q <= count_q + 1; // 32-bit unsized literal '1' causes WIDTHTRUNC!

candidate_rules.summary: Break circular combinational feedback loops (UNOPTFLAT) by registering the feedback state in an always_ff sequential element.
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: A combinational signal that depends on itself without an intervening flip-flop forms an asynchronous ring oscillator or unstable bistable latch in silicon, preventing Verilator static scheduling (UNOPTFLAT), hanging event-driven simulators, and breaking static timing analysis.
candidate_rules.anti_pattern:
// [ANTI-PATTERN] Combinational net 'acc_w' feeds back into its own equation
assign acc_w = in_i ^ acc_w;
candidate_rules.sdc_constraint: N/A (Combinational loops are illegal in synchronous STA)

candidate_rules.summary: Never use blocking assignments (=) on sequential registers inside always_ff; strictly use non-blocking assignments (<=).
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: Using blocking assignments (=) inside a clocked always_ff block causes the simulator to update the LHS variable in the Active region rather than the NBA (Non-Blocking Assignment) region. Any downstream sequential block reading that signal on the same clock edge will sample the post-edge value instead of the pre-edge value, creating a severe simulation-vs-synthesis mismatch.
candidate_rules.anti_pattern:
always_ff @(posedge clk_i) begin
  stage1_q = data_i;   // %Warning-BLKSEQ!
  stage2_q = stage1_q; // Collapses 2-stage pipeline into 1 stage!
end

candidate_rules.summary: Avoid overlapping casez patterns and never use synopsys full_case/parallel_case pragmas; use explicit mutually exclusive branches with a default clause.
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: Overlapping case items or synthesis pragmas (full_case / parallel_case) cause synthesis tools to optimize logic differently from how event-driven RTL simulators evaluate top-down case branches, producing catastrophic gate-level functional divergence.
candidate_rules.anti_pattern:
always_comb begin
  casez (req_i)
    2'b1?: grant_o = 2'b10;
    2'b?1: grant_o = 2'b01; // Overlaps with 2'b11 (%Warning-CASEOVERLAP)!
    default: grant_o = 2'b00;
  endcase
end

candidate_rules.summary: Replace deep serial priority chains and linear ripple comparators with balanced binary tree reductions to minimize Yosys ltp -noff critical path levels across Sky130, Nangate45, and ASAP7.
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: Linearly cascaded priority multiplexers or ripple comparators synthesize into O(N) gate levels in Yosys ABC. Restructuring associative operations (min/max sorters, wide reductions, parallel muxes) into explicit balanced binary trees compresses combinational logic depth to O(log2 N).

candidate_rules.summary: Mux operands before a single shared adder/subtractor rather than instantiating parallel arithmetic units followed by an output mux to reduce standard-cell area (chip_area_um2).
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: Instantiating separate adders in each branch of an if-else statement forces synthesis to build two full carry-propagate adders plus a wide bus multiplexer. Selecting the input operand via a 2:1 mux before a single adder cuts arithmetic silicon area nearly in half.
candidate_rules.anti_pattern:
// [ANTI-PATTERN] Two separate adders synthesized before output MUX
assign res_o = sel_i ? (base_i + offset_a_i) : (base_i + offset_b_i);

candidate_rules.summary: Size datapath accumulators, loop counters, and LLR path metrics to the exact mathematical dynamic range ceiling ($\lceil\log_2(\text{MAX})\rceil$) rather than defaulting to 32-bit integers.
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: Using 32-bit int/integer registers for counters or channel decoder path metrics that only span [0..63] wastes 26 flip-flops per register and inflates comparator/sorter trees by 5x in cell count and dynamic toggle power.
candidate_rules.anti_pattern:
// [ANTI-PATTERN] 32-bit integer register used for a 0..7 bit index counter
int bit_idx_q;

candidate_rules.summary: Gate combinational datapath inputs (operand isolation) and enable-gate output registers when a submodule is idle to minimize bit-level Hamming toggles in power_activity.json.
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: If a wide combinational sorter or ALU remains directly connected to toggling bus nets during FSM states where its output is ignored, every internal gate charges and discharges load capacitance unnecessarily, inflating total_bit_hamming_toggles.
candidate_rules.anti_pattern:
// [ANTI-PATTERN] Wide sorter/adder toggles every cycle even when valid_i is 0
assign sum_o = data_a_i + data_b_i;

candidate_rules.summary: Guard valid control strobes and FSM state registers against X/Z unknown propagation after reset deassertion using !$isunknown() checks.
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: In 4-state SystemVerilog simulation, an uninitialized register or out-of-bounds array read evaluates to 'X'. In standard if (cond) blocks, 'X' takes the else branch (X-optimism), silently hiding hardware reset bugs unless caught by x_z_anomalies or ASSERT_KNOWN.
candidate_rules.anti_pattern:
// [ANTI-PATTERN] Unreset control valid register propagates X onto the bus
always_ff @(posedge clk_i) valid_q <= next_valid_d;

candidate_rules.summary: Declare unrelated clock domains using set_clock_groups -asynchronous only after verifying that all boundary crossings have hardware CDC synchronizers.
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: Static Timing Analysis (STA) engines cannot meaningfully compute setup/hold slack between two clocks with an irrational or asynchronous phase relationship (e.g., 10.0ns vs 31.7ns). Applying set_clock_groups -asynchronous instructs STA to ignore cross-domain paths so synthesis does not waste buffer area trying to close unclosable paths.
candidate_rules.anti_pattern:
# [ANTI-PATTERN] Leaving asynchronous clocks unconstrained or using blanket set_false_path without clock groups
create_clock -name clkA -period 10.0 [get_ports clkA]
create_clock -name clkB -period 31.7 [get_ports clkB]
candidate_rules.golden_template:
# [GOLDEN PATTERN] Master clock declarations + asynchronous clock group isolation
create_clock -name clkA -period 10.0 [get_ports clkA]
create_clock -name clkB -period 31.7 [get_ports clkB]
set_clock_groups -asynchronous -group [get_clocks clkA] -group [get_clocks clkB]

candidate_rules.summary: Constrain multi-bit Gray-code FIFO pointers with set_max_delay -datapath_only bounded to less than one source clock period to prevent multi-bit skew violations.
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: Although Gray code changes only 1 bit per source clock cycle, if physical routing delay skew across the N pointer wires exceeds 1 source clock period (T_src), two sequential bit transitions from Cycle k and Cycle k+1 can arrive at the destination synchronizer simultaneously, defeating the Gray-code guarantee.
candidate_rules.anti_pattern:
# [ANTI-PATTERN] Using unrestricted set_false_path on a multi-bit Gray-code pointer bus allows arbitrary wire skew!
set_false_path -from [get_cells wptr_gray_q*] -to [get_cells wq1_rptr*]
candidate_rules.golden_template:
# [GOLDEN PATTERN] Bound datapath routing delay across Gray pointer bits to <= 0.8 * T_src
set_max_delay 8.0 -datapath_only -from [get_pins wptr_gray_q*/Q] -to [get_pins wq1_rptr*/D]

candidate_rules.summary: Synchronize asynchronous reset deassertion via a 2-FF reset bridge and apply set_false_path only to the asynchronous assertion pin.
candidate_rules.hardware_rationale: While asynchronous reset assertion is timing-independent, asynchronous reset deassertion near an active clock edge violates flip-flop recovery time (t_rec), throwing registers into metastability. A 2-FF reset synchronizer asserts asynchronously and deasserts synchronously.
candidate_rules.anti_pattern: // [ANTI-PATTERN] Feeding raw external pad reset directly into internal FSM flip-flops without a reset synchronizer
